AGENCY:

SUMMARY:
The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) finds that revocation of the countervailing duty (CVD) order on phosphate fertilizers (fertilizers) from the Kingdom of Morocco (Morocco) would likely to lead to the continuation or recurrence of a countervailable subsidy at the levels indicated in the “Final Results of Sunset Review” section of this notice.
DATES:
Applicable November 3, 2026.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Faris Montgomery, AD/CVD Operations, Office VIII, Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, U.S. Department of Commerce, 1401 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20230; telephone: (202) 482-1537.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Background
On April 7, 2021, Commerce published a CVD order on fertilizers from Morocco.[1]
On March 2, 2026, Commerce published the notice of initiation of the first sunset review of the
Order,
pursuant to section 751(c) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (the Act), and 19 CFR 351.218(c).[2]
On the basis of notices of intent to participate and adequate substantive responses filed by domestic interested parties, and adequate responses from the Government of Morocco (GOM) and respondent OCP S.A. (OCP), Commerce determined to conduct a full sunset review of this CVD order, pursuant to section 751(c) of the Act and 19 CFR 351.218(e)(2).[3]
On July 24, 2026, Commerce preliminarily determined that revocation of the CVD order on phosphate fertilizers from Morocco would likely lead to continuation or recurrence of subsidization.[4]
On August 24, 2026, the GOM and OCP filed case briefs in response to the
Preliminary Results.[5]
On August 31, 2026, Commerce received rebuttal briefs from domestic interested parties, the Mosaic Company (Mosaic) and J.R. Simplot Company, LLC (Simplot).[6]
Scope of the Order
The product covered by the
Order
is fertilizers from Morocco. For a full description of the scope,
see

AGENCY:
Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, Department of Commerce.
SUMMARY:
On October 19, 2026, the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) Secretariat issued a Notice of Final Panel Action. The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) is notifying the public that the NAFTA Binational Panel's final judgment is not in harmony with Commerce's final determination in the countervailing duty (CVD) investigation of certain softwood lumber products (lumber) from Canada, and that Commerce is amending the final determination and the resulting CVD order with respect to the countervailable subsidy rate assigned to Canfor Corporation (Canfor); J.D. Irving, Limited (J.D. Irving); Resolute FP Canada Inc. (Resolute); Tolko Marketing and Sales Ltd. (Tolko); West Fraser Mills Ltd. (West Fraser); and all other companies.
DATES:
Applicable October 29, 2026.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Samuel Brummitt, AD/CVD Operations, Office III, Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, U.S. Department of Commerce, 1401 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20230; telephone: (202) 482-7851.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Background
On November 8, 2017, Commerce published its
Final Determination
in the CVD investigation of lumber from Canada.[1]
The
Final Determination
was subsequently amended.[2]
Respondent parties subsequently challenged Commerce's final determination before the NAFTA Binational Panel, pursuant to Article 1904 of NAFTA. The parties briefed and argued the case before the Panel and, on March 6, 2024, the Panel issued its decision, affirming in part and remanding in part Commerce's determination.[3]
On December 17, 2024, Commerce issued its
First Remand Determination.[4]
On March 6, 2026, the Panel issued its decision on remand, affirming in part and remanding in part Commerce's
First Remand Determination.[5]
On June 17, 2026, Commerce issued its
Second Remand Determination.[6]
By decision on October 5, 2026, the NAFTA Panel affirmed Commerce's
Second Remand Determination.[7]
On October 19, 2026, the Panel directed the NAFTA Secretariat to issue a Notice of Final Panel Action; the NAFTA Secretariat subsequently issued the Notice of Final Panel Action on October 19, 2026.
Timken Notice
In its decision in
Timken,[8]
as clarified by
Diamond Sawblades,[9]
the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit held that, pursuant to sections 516A(c) and (e) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (the Act), Commerce must publish a notice of court decision that is not “in harmony” with a Commerce determination and must suspend liquidation of entries pending a “conclusive” court decision. Because NAFTA panels step into the shoes of the courts they are replacing, they must apply the law of the national court that would otherwise review the administrative determination. Therefore, we are publishing notice that the NAFTA Panel's Panel Decision on Second Remand, as memorialized by the NAFTA Secretariat's October 19, 2026, Notice of Final Panel Action, is “not in harmony” with the
Final Determination.[10]
Publication of this notice fulfills the obligation imposed upon Commerce by the decision in
Timken.
Amended Final Determination

articles.title: Trade deficit has eased, falling to just over $12 billion in the first 10 months. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Trade deficit has eased, falling to just over $12 billion in the first 10 months.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Vietnam's import and export turnover has surpassed the $1 trillion mark. This milestone was once again confirmed after the General Statistics Office ( Ministry of Finance ) officially released economic data for October and the first 10 months of 2026.
 According to the General Statistics Office, in the first 10 months of 2026, the total value of goods exports and imports reached a preliminary figure of US$1,010.55 billion, an increase of 32.3% compared to the same period last year.
 "This is the first time Vietnam's total import and export turnover of goods has exceeded the $1 trillion mark, reaching an all-time high, demonstrating that the scale of international trade continues to expand strongly," the General Statistics Office stated .
 Within this record figure, exports reached $499.24 billion, a 27.5% increase compared to the same period last year; imports reached $511.31 billion, a 37.4% increase compared to the same period last year. 
|  | 
| Vietnam's merchandise trade in the first 10 months of 2026 | 
 Due to imports increasing faster than exports, the trade balance for goods showed a deficit of US$12.07 billion (compared to a surplus of US$19.49 billion in the same period last year). Of this, the domestic economic sector had a deficit of US$37.83 billion; while the foreign-invested sector (including crude oil) had a surplus of US$25.76 billion.
 Thus, the trade deficit has cooled down, alleviating concerns about the trade imbalance in recent months. In fact, a trade surplus has returned. In September 2026, the surplus was $1.3 billion. In October 2026, the surplus reached $7.31 billion. If this trend continues, the merchandise trade balance will continue to improve in the coming months.
 Returning to the import and export situation, data from the General Statistics Office shows that merchandise exports in October 2026 reached US$64.67 billion, an increase of 8.7% compared to the previous month. This brings the total merchandise exports for the first 10 months of 2026 to US$499.24 billion, an increase of 27.5% compared to the same period last year.
 Of this total, the domestic economic sector achieved $93.93 billion, an increase of 8.2%, accounting for 18.8% of total export turnover; the foreign-invested sector (including crude oil) reached $405.31 billion, an increase of 33%, accounting for 81.2%. Thus, the foreign-invested sector continues to make a significant contribution to the country's total merchandise export turnover.
 In the first 10 months of 2026, 37 product categories achieved export turnover exceeding 1 billion USD, accounting for 94.9% of total export turnover. Of these, 8 product categories exceeded 10 billion USD in export value, accounting for 73.4%.
 Specifically, exports of electronics, computers and components reached over $149.4 billion, an increase of 71% compared to the same period last year. Exports of machinery, equipment, tools and other spare parts reached over $63.2 billion, an increase of 30.4%; telephones and components $57.6 billion, an increase of 18.4%; textiles and garments $33.735 billion, an increase of 2.2%; footwear $20.24 billion; transport vehicles and parts $16.74 billion, an increase of 17.1%...
 Conversely, in October 2026, import turnover reached US$57.36 billion, a decrease of 1.4% compared to the previous month, bringing the total import turnover for the first 10 months to US$511.31 billion, an increase of 37.4% compared to the same period last year. Of this, the domestic economic sector accounted for US$131.76 billion, an increase of 23%; and the foreign-invested sector accounted for US$379.55 billion, an increase of 43.2%. 
|  | 
| Electronics, computers, and components are currently Vietnam's largest export items in terms of value. | 
 Statistics also show that in the first 10 months of 2026, 47 imported items reached a value of over 1 billion USD, accounting for 95.0% of total import turnover. Of these, 8 imported items exceeded 10 billion USD, accounting for 67.3%.
 The largest imports belonged to the electronics, computer and components group, reaching $215.25 billion, an increase of 74.4% compared to the same period last year. Meanwhile, imports of machinery, equipment, tools and other spare parts exceeded $60 billion; imports of textiles reached $12.875 billion; and imports of petroleum products reached $10.244 billion…
 In terms of structure, the group of production materials reached US$481.03 billion, accounting for 94.1% of total import turnover. Of this, machinery, equipment, tools and spare parts accounted for 58.5%; raw materials, fuels and materials accounted for 35.6%. The group of consumer goods reached US$30.28 billion, accounting for 5.9%. This import structure is healthy, mainly importing to serve domestic production needs.
 In terms of markets, the United States is Vietnam's largest export market with a turnover of $159.40 billion. China is Vietnam's largest import market with a turnover of $212.46 billion.
 In the first 10 months of 2026, Vietnam's trade surplus with the United States was $140.10 billion, up 26.2% year-on-year; with the EU $40.84 billion, up 26.8%; and with Japan $3.42 billion, up 110.4%. Conversely, the trade deficit with China was $134.94 billion, up 43.2%; with South Korea $48.63 billion, up 91.1%; and with ASEAN $16.93 billion, up 46%.

articles.full_text:
US tech stocks made a recovery on Tuesday afternoon after a selloff spooked investors over AI spending.
Tuesday’s midterm elections didn’t appear to have a huge impact on Wall Street, though investors are predicting Democrats get at least a majority in the House and potentially gain seats in the Senate, which could lead to more AI regulation.
The S&P 500 was up 0.37% at market closing on Tuesday, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq increased 0.83% for the day. The Dow dropped 0.38% following a 1.9% dip in Apple’s share price after the company released a worse-than-expected margin forecast due to the higher cost of memory chips.
Nvidia picked up a 2.3% gain after dropping over four sessions, while fellow chipmakers Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom and Micron Technology also jumped on Tuesday.
Tuesday marked the end of a brief selloff of AI and tech stocks that started last week, with the Nasdaq in October experiencing its largest monthly decline since March 2025. The Nasdaq had ended on Monday in correction territory, dropping 10% from its 6 October record close.
Small drops in oil prices, amid potential new negotiations with Iran and Russia, also eased investors. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, dropped to $103 a barrel on Tuesday, down from $117 a barrel at the end of October.
While many Americans say frustration with the higher cost of living will be a major factor in their vote on Tuesday, Wall Street has continued to soar off investments in AI, particularly the chips and infrastructure used to power the technology. The S&P 500 is up 10% for the year so far, while the Nasdaq and the Dow are up 9% and 7%, respectively.
Analysis from CNBC of post-midterms market performance from 1980 to 2024 showed the market tends to pick up after an election. Wall Street is often jittery before an election, when results are uncertain, but tends to recover once results are settled.

articles.title: UK’s most polluting power plant could power country’s largest AI datacentre
articles.summary: Drax’s FTSE 250 owner strikes £20bn deal to build infrastructure in what it says is site’s ‘next chapter’Britain’s most polluting power plant could soon power the country’s largest datacentre under a £20bn deal to build AI infrastructure on the site of the Drax power plant in North Yorkshire.The power plant’s FTSE 250 owner has struck a deal with the infrastructure investor Brookfield and ⁠and the AI infrastructure platform Radiant to develop a datacentre with an eventual capacity of more than 1...
articles.full_text:
Britain’s most polluting power plant could soon power the country’s largest datacentre under a £20bn deal to build AI infrastructure on the site of the Drax power plant in North Yorkshire.
The power plant’s FTSE 250 owner has struck a deal with the infrastructure investor Brookfield and and the AI infrastructure platform Radiant to develop a datacentre with an eventual capacity of more than 1 gigawatt that could begin operations by early 2028.
In the initial phase, Drax will provide the datacentre project with land and access to the national power grid through existing connections on the site, but it hopes to begin powering the datacentre directly by the early 2030s.
Drax said the development could attract more than £20bn ($26.8bn) in investment and represent “the next chapter” for the former power plant after ministers signalled plans to limit its power generation in the future.
The Drax chief executive, Will Gardiner, said the project would “help secure the long-term future of the site and protect hundreds of jobs” while “supporting the north’s reindustrialisation and strengthening sovereign AI capability”.
The largest power plant in the UK produces almost 5% of the country’s electricity by burning woody biomass pellets, making the site the single largest emitter of carbon dioxide, according to analysts.
These emissions are not accounted for by the UK government because Drax claims the equivalent carbon emissions are absorbed by growing trees that provide the waste wood used to make the biomass pellets.
However, the government promised that Drax would play a “much more limited role” in future after growing concerns over the company’s sustainability claims, and will have access to only half its current £2m a day subsidies from 2027 to 2031.
The company hopes to clear the regulatory approvals needed to begin supplying the datacentre directly before 2031 to secure its future revenues. The news was welcomed by equity analysts, while the company’s market value climbed by almost 9% on the London Stock Exchange to almost £3bn.
Under phase one of the project, the datacentre would be operational from the first quarter of 2028 with up to 100MW of compute capacity.
The deal has emerged a week after the government published a draft national policy statement on datacentres, which said they were “as fundamental to our economy as the railways and electricity networks on which we have long depended”.
“We must take control over the development of datacentres in this country and ensure that the country and host communities benefit from them,” the government said.
However, the UK’s congested grid infrastructure and ambitious legally binding climate targets have raised questions over how a dash to build datacentres could be powered without relying heavily on expensive and polluting off-grid gas generation.

articles.title: Apple warns of ‘unprecedented’ rise in memory chip prices
articles.summary: iPhone maker says decision to raise prices has offset some of impact, as revenues are stronger than expectedBusiness live – latest updatesApple has warned of an “unprecedented” rise in memory chip prices, as it battles with datacentres to lay its hands on supplies.The iPhone maker’s shares fell in after-hours trading after it told investors that the higher prices will eat into its profit margins. Continue reading...
articles.full_text:
Apple has warned of an “unprecedented” rise in memory chip prices, as it battles with datacentres to lay its hands on supplies.
The iPhone maker’s shares fell in after-hours trading after it told investors that the higher prices will eat into its profit margins.
“What we’re seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented,” John Ternus, Apple’s new chief executive, told a conference call on Monday, predicting that memory costs in the fourth quarter of this year would be even higher than in the previous three months.
The tech industry has been gripped by “RAMageddon” for months, as demand for memory chips from AI datacentres has surged, driving up prices.
Ternus said Apple’s decision to raise iPad and MacBook prices in June, followed by iPhone prices in September, had “provided some offset” for the company.
Ben Barringer, the head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot, said Apple’s results were “OK, if on the disappointing side”.
“Revenues were up 12%, driven primarily by iPhone sales and strong sales of Mac Mini, which users can use to apply agentic AI. China growth was robust which is pleasing to see, while iPad and wearables disappointed with services growing but lower than the group average at 10%,” he added.
“There appears to be a lot of interest in the iPhone Duo, but it is early days yet with the product not yet on full release, but it is hoped that can help drive the next leg of Apple’s product innovation.”
Apple’s shares were down 2.75% in after-hours trading on Wall Street.
Apple posted stronger-than-expected revenue in the fiscal third quarter, giving Ternus an upbeat start to his tenure, which began in September. The solid results bucked a downward trend for tech companies this quarter, as companies including Alphabet, Amazon and Intel had disappointing quarterly results.
Jacob Bourne, an Emarketer analyst, said record iPhone revenue and strong growth in China demonstrated the resilience of Apple’s business.
Apple earned $30.71bn (£22.89bn), or $2.10 a share, in the July-September period, up 12% from $27.47bn, or $1.85 a share, in the equivalent period a year earlier. Apple said its earnings included five cents a share from tariff refunds.
Revenue rose 12% to $114.5bn from $102.5bn.
Analysts, on average, were expecting earnings of $1.99 a share on revenue of $113.4bn, according to a poll by FactSet.
While its rivals are facing investor uncertainty over huge investments in artificial intelligence, Bourne said Apple’s “tepid approach” to AI infrastructure spending had helped preserve its cashflow – while partnerships with companies such as Alphabet could help the iPhone maker strengthen its AI capabilities without taking on the same financial risks as its peers.

articles.title: Foreign-Trade Zone 168; Application for Subzone; Samsung Electro-Mechanics America, Inc.; Wilmer, Texas

An application has been submitted to the Foreign-Trade Zones (FTZ) Board by the Metroplex International Trade Development Corporation, grantee of FTZ 168, requesting subzone status for the facility of Samsung Electro-Mechanics America, Inc., located in Wilmer, Texas. The application was submitted pursuant to the provisions of the Foreign-Trade Zones Act, as amended (19 U.S.C. 81a-81u), and the regulations of the FTZ Board (15 CFR part 400). It was formally docketed on October 28, 2026.
The proposed subzone (0.69 acres) is located at 1200 Fulghum Road, Wilmer, Texas. No authorization for production activity has been requested at this time. The proposed subzone would be subject to the existing activation limit of FTZ 168.
In accordance with the FTZ Board's regulations, Camille Evans of the FTZ Staff is designated examiner to review the application and make recommendations to the Executive Secretary.
                    Public comment is invited from interested parties. Submissions shall be addressed to the FTZ Board's Executive Secretary and sent to: 
                    ftz@trade.gov.

                    A copy of the application will be available for public inspection in the “Online FTZ Information System” section of the FTZ Board's website, which is accessible via 
                    www.trade.gov/ftz.

articles.full_text: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of a final guidance titled "Potency Assurance for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products." The guidance document provides recommendations to help assure the potency of human cellular therapy or gene therapy (CGT) products at all stages of the product lifecycle. FDA is recommending a comprehensive approach to potency assurance of CGT products that is grounded in quality risk management. For investigational products, we describe how to progressively implement a strategy for potency assurance during product development and provide additional considerations to help assure the potency of products that are undergoing rapid clinical development. For licensed products, we describe requirements for potency assurance, including testing required for lot release assays. The guidance announced in this notice finalizes the draft guidance of the same title issued on December 28, 2023.

AGENCY:
National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Commerce.
ACTION:
Notice of public hearings and comment period.
SUMMARY:
NMFS will hold five public hearings in November and December 2026 to solicit input on a potential Secretarial amendment to the Atlantic Sea Scallop Fishery Management Plan. If the Secretary of Commerce determines that such an amendment is warranted, the action would consider allowing permit stacking in the limited access scallop fleet. NMFS is soliciting written scoping comments on this topic.
DATES:
Public hearing will be held in November and December 2026. Comments are due on January 4, 2027. See
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION
for specific hearing dates.
ADDRESSES:
See
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION
for hearing addresses.
You may submit comments on this document, identified by NOAA-NMFS-2026-3136, by any of the following methods:
Electronic Submission:
Submit all electronic public comments via the Federal e-Rulemaking Portal. Visit
https://www.regulations.gov
and type NOAA-NMFS-2026-3136 in the Search box. Click on the “Comment” icon, complete the required fields, and enter or attach your comments.
Mail:
Submit written comments to Emily Keiley, 55 Great Republic Drive, Gloucester, MA 01930.
Instructions:
Comments sent by any other method, to any other address or individual, or received after the end of the comment period, may not be considered by NMFS. All comments received are a part of the public record and will generally be posted for public viewing on
https://www.regulations.gov
without change. All personal identifying information (
e.g.,
name, address), confidential business information, or otherwise sensitive information submitted voluntarily by the sender will be publicly accessible. NMFS will accept anonymous comments (enter “N/A” in the required fields if you wish to remain anonymous).
Hearing Locations—NMFS will hold two online webinars and three in-person public hearings:
1.
Tuesday, November 17, 2026, 4 p.m. to 6 p.m.;
Hilton Garden Inn Boston Logan Airport, 100 Boardman St., Boston, MA 02128; phone (617) 567-6789. Note: The Scoping Meeting will begin 30 minutes after the conclusion of the Joint Scallop Committee and Advisory Panel Meeting.
5.
Monday, December 14, 2026, 1 p.m. to 3 p.m.;
University of Massachusetts Dartmouth School for Marine Science and Technology East, 836 South Rodney French Blvd., New Bedford, MA 02744; phone: (508) 999-8193.
Background
Based on comments received in response to Executive Order 14276, the Secretary of Commerce is considering whether to develop an amendment to the Atlantic Scallop Fishery Management Plan (FMP) to allow permit stacking in the limited access scallop fishery. The publication of this
Federal Register
notice does not commit the Secretary to take action at this time, but is intended to notify the public of the opportunity to be heard and that NMFS, on behalf of the Secretary, is soliciting feedback to inform the Secretary's decision whether to develop an amendment for permit stacking.
The New England Fishery Management Council (Council) established the Limited Access component of the sea scallop fishery through Amendment 4 (1994) to the Atlantic Sea Scallop FMP. This action was part of an effort control program designed to reduce fishing mortality and rebuild the scallop resource in what was, at that time, an overfished stock. Amendment 4 included measures designed to limit increases in a vessel's fishing power and reduce fishing pressure, such as limiting fishing time through days-at-sea (DAS) management, crew restrictions, gear restrictions, reporting requirements, and vessel upgrade restrictions.
Excess capacity remains in the limited access scallop fishery; that is, the capacity of individual vessels and the fleet as a whole is greater than what is needed to efficiently harvest sustainable levels of catch. Since the limited access program was implemented in 1994, the annual allocation of DAS has reduced steadily. Due to effort reductions in Amendment 4 (1994) and Amendment 7 (1999), DAS allocations were reduced almost by half from 204 DAS in 1994 to 120 DAS in 1999. Since 1999, the number of open area DAS has continued
( printed page 69244)
to decline, although more effort has been allocated to fish in access areas, which served to offset that reduction. In fishing year 2026, a full-time vessel was allocated 36 open area DAS and no access area trips.
Some members of the industry have commented that the current low allocations, paired with increasing costs, are reducing profits and suggesting the reconsideration of certain management approaches may be timely. Some crews routinely work on multiple vessels in one fishing year. Further, reports suggest that some ports are congested with vessels tied to the dock for the majority of the year causing safety and space issues.
The Secretary is considering addressing excess capacity in the limited access scallop fishing by allowing up to two limited access scallop permits to be combined on a single vessel. The vessel would be permitted to fish the allocations for both permits, which would reduce business expenses associated with maintaining multiple vessels with low DAS allocations.
To mitigate risks of fleet consolidation, job loss, and effort spillover into other fisheries, any potential Secretarial amendment under consideration would evaluate specific protective management measures, including but not limited to:
Limiting stacked permits to those within the same Limited Access category (i.e.,
full-time, part-time, occasional);
Requiring stacking to be a one-time, permanent, and irreversible action (i.e.,
prohibiting de-stacking);
Whether to restrict permit stacking to strictly respect existing vessel length, tonnage, and horsepower baseline restrictions (i.e.,
disallowing a permit carrying a smaller baseline specification to stack onto a vessel with larger baselines and to ensure stacking is not used to bypass vessel replacement limits);
Narrowing allowable permit stacking exclusively to vessels under common ownership or common control in order to avoid fleet concentration and accommodate the needs of active owner-operators; and
Maintaining the ownership cap of no more than 5 percent of the total number of limited access permits.
These hearings are physically accessible to people with disabilities. Requests for sign language interpretation or other auxiliary aid should be directed to Emily Keiley, (978) 281-9116 at least 5 days prior to any meeting date.

articles.full_text: The National Center of Excellence for Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) Safety (National LNG Center) will host a series of informational workshops on best practices for LNG safety titled, "LNG Safety Best Practices Workshop." The workshops are free; will be hosted in-person with select hybrid sessions offered virtually; and will require advance registration. Each workshop will be a full day and will cover a variety of best practices each session. PHMSA established the National LNG Center in 2023 pursuant to section 111 of the Protecting Our Infrastructure of Pipelines and Enhancing Safety (PIPES) Act of 2020 (Pub. L. 116-260), which directs the National LNG Center to advance Federal LNG expertise, serve as a repository of best practices, and facilitate collaboration among LNG stakeholders. Consistent with this mandate, the workshop series will bring together representatives from industry, government, academia, emergency response organizations, and other stakeholders to promote information sharing and continuous improvement in LNG safety.

AGENCY:
Office of the Deputy Secretary, HUD.
ACTION:
Notice of waiver.
SUMMARY:
This notice announces a waiver, granted by the Secretary, through the Deputy Secretary, of the minimum 30-day application period required under section 102(a) of the HUD Reform Act for the FY2026 Continuum of Care Program (CoC) notice of funding opportunity (NOFO), which was re-opened for application submission on September 18, 2026 (CPD-2600-DC-0025).
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
For information regarding this notice, contact Claudette Fernandez, General Deputy Assistant Secretary for the Office of Community Planning and Development, Department of Housing and Urban Development, 451 7th Street SW, Washington, DC 20410; telephone number (202) 402-6009 (this is not a toll-free number); email
CoCNOFO@HUD.gov.
HUD welcomes and is prepared to receive calls from individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as individuals with speech and communication disabilities. To learn more about how to make an accessible telephone call, please visit
https://www.fcc.gov/consumers/guides/telecommunications-relay-service-trs.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Section 102(a) of the HUD Reform Act (42 U.S.C.
( printed page 69268)
3545(a)) sets out the requirements for notice to the public regarding assistance available from HUD. Section 102(a)(3) requires publication of selection criteria not less than 30 days before the deadline for applications or requests for assistance. HUD may waive this requirement if “the Secretary determines that the waiver is required for appropriate response to an emergency.” If HUD makes an emergency waiver, then it must publish “the Secretary's reasons for doing so” in the
Federal Register
within 30 days. HUD does not believe that it must seek an emergency waiver for the FY2026 CoC NOFO, but is doing so out of an abundance of caution for the reasons below.
Due to litigation, the FY2026 CoC NOFO has been published, vacated, and restored over recent months.
On June 1, 2026, HUD published the FY2026 CoC NOFO with an August 26, 2026, application deadline, which gave applicants 87 days to review the NOFO and submit applications. HUD subsequently published a modified NOFO on July 24, 2026, which maintained an August 26, 2026, application deadline and made no substantive changes apart from adding a mechanism for direct-to-HUD funding for areas with no collaborative applicant, as spelled out in Appendix III of the NOFO.
In early July, two groups of plaintiffs sued to challenge the NOFO in the United States District Court for the District of Rhode Island. On August 7, the district court vacated the FY26 NOFO. ECF 41,
State of Washington
v.
HUD,
1:26-cv-439 (D.R.I.); ECF 34,
Nat'l All. To End Homelessness
v.
HUD,
1:26-cv-436 (D.R.I.). The NOFO was thus rendered null and void less than 20 days before the original deadline. HUD appealed the ruling. During the appeal, HUD maintained a copy of the NOFO on its website [
https://www.hud.gov/hud-partners/coc-program-competition] and sent a listserv message to applicants notifying them of the same.
And on September 16, 2026, the United States Court of Appeals for the First Circuit stayed the lower court's judgment while the Plaintiffs' challenge to the NOFO proceeds.
State of Washington
v.
HUD,
__F.4th__, 2026 WL 2730937 (1st Cir. 2026). As a result, the NOFO was automatically restored.
See
NOFO at 111.
On September 18, 2026, the Department re-opened the FY2026 CoC NOFO (CPD-2600-DC-0025), with a funding application deadline of 8:00 p.m. ET on September 30, 2026, which created an additional 12-day application window to resume the competition that was paused 68 days after publication of the June 1 NOFO. The additional period was less than the 30-day minimum application requirement under section 102(a)(3). But it is part of the larger application period of 80 days, so HUD does not believe that the NOFO requires an emergency waiver under section 102(a)(3). Still, the Secretary has determined that it is nevertheless prudent to issue a waiver.
It was necessary for the Department to establish a short application reopening period for this NOFO to address certain exigent and emergency circumstances. Specifically, HUD is required by Congress to make awards under the NOFO by December 1, 2026. HUD also endeavors to make timely awards to ensure ongoing funding for successful and meritorious projects, and for other projects that the CoCs or Congress may lawfully protect from competition.
HUD established the original August 26 application deadline to build in the necessary amount of time it reasonably expected it would need to review several thousands of applications and make awards. But the District Court ruling, which is now vacated, eliminated part of the approximately 90-day application period HUD originally provided. HUD must now process all applications and make awards within 62 days, which would be the quickest that the program has ever processed applications. It has received close to 8,000 individual project applications, including 3,500 new project applications, and almost 400 CoC applications. Historically, application reviews have required over 90 days to complete, so it cannot afford to lengthen the general application deadline any further.
Applicants have had nearly four months to review the NOFO and prepare applications, so an additional 12-day application period is sufficient time for applicants to finalize and submit their applications while also reserving for HUD time needed to meet the congressionally mandated December 1 deadline. As such, the circumstances demonstrated that an emergency existed that justified the granting of a waiver of the 30-day application period required under section 102(a) of the HUD Reform Act.

AGENCY:
Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), Treasury.
ACTION:
Notice and request for comment.
SUMMARY:
The OCC, as part of its continuing effort to reduce paperwork and respondent burden, invites comment on a continuing information collection, as required by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA). In accordance with the requirements of the PRA, the OCC may not conduct or sponsor, and the respondent is not required to respond to, an information collection unless it displays a currently valid Office of Management and Budget (OMB) control number. The OCC is soliciting comment concerning the renewal of its information collection titled, “Mandatory Contractual Stay Requirements for Qualified Financial Contracts.”
DATES:
Comments must be received by January 4, 2027.
ADDRESSES:
Commenters are encouraged to submit comments by email, if possible. You may submit comments by any of the following methods:
Mail:
Chief Counsel's Office, Attention: Comment Processing, Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, Attention: 1557-0339, 400 7th Street SW, Suite 1E-216, Washington, DC 20219.
Hand Delivery/Courier:
400 7th Street SW, Suite 1E-216, Washington, DC 20219.
Fax:
(571) 293-4835.
Instructions:
You must include “OCC” as the agency name and “1557-0339” in your comment. In general, the OCC will publish comments on
www.reginfo.gov
without change, including any business or personal information provided, such as name and address information, email addresses, or phone numbers. Comments received, including attachments and other supporting materials, are part of the public record and subject to public disclosure. Do not include any information in your comment or supporting materials that you consider confidential or inappropriate for public disclosure.
( printed page 69310)
Following the close of this notice's 60-day comment period, the OCC will publish a second notice with a 30-day comment period. You may review comments and other related materials that pertain to this information collection beginning on the date of publication of the second notice for this collection by the method set forth in the next bullet.
Viewing Comments Electronically:
Go to
www.reginfo.gov.
Hover over the “Information Collection Review” tab and click on “Information Collection Review” from the drop-down menu. From the “Currently under Review” drop-down menu, select “Department of the Treasury” and then click “submit.” This information collection can be located by searching OMB control number “1557-0339” or “Mandatory Contractual Stay Requirements for Qualified Financial Contracts.” Upon finding the appropriate information collection, click on the related “ICR Reference Number.” On the next screen, select “View Supporting Statement and Other Documents” and then click on the link to any comment listed at the bottom of the screen.
For assistance in navigating
www.reginfo.gov,
please contact the Regulatory Information Service Center at (202) 482-7340.

Shaquita Merritt, Clearance Officer, (202) 649-5490, Chief Counsel's Office, Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, 400 7th Street SW, Washington, DC 20219. If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability, please dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.

Under the PRA (44 U.S.C. 3501et seq.), Federal agencies must obtain approval from the OMB for each collection of information that they conduct or sponsor. “Collection of information” is defined in 44 U.S.C. 3502(3) and 5 CFR 1320.3(c) to include agency requests or requirements, imposed on ten or more persons, that members of the public submit reports, keep records, or provide information to a third party. Section 3506(c)(2)(A) of title 44 generally requires Federal agencies to provide a 60-day notice in the
Federal Register
concerning each proposed collection of information, including each proposed extension of an existing collection of information, before submitting the collection to OMB for approval. To comply with this requirement, the OCC is publishing notice of the renewal of this collection.

articles.title: Public Utility District No. 1 of Chelan County, Washington; Notice of Applications for Approval of Contracts for the Sale of Power Under Section 22 of the Federal Power Act
articles.full_text:
Take notice that on October 16, 2026, Public Utility District No. 1 of Chelan County, Washington (Chelan PUD) filed with the Commission three applications for approval of contracts for the sale of power from its licensed Rock Island Hydroelectric Project No. 943 for periods beyond the expiration of its existing license for the project.[] 
                    
                     The project is located on the Columbia River in Chelan and Douglas Counties, Washington.
                
Section 22 of the Federal Power Act, 16 U.S.C. 815, provides that contracts for the sale and delivery of power for periods extending beyond the termination date of a license may be entered into upon the joint approval of the Commission and the appropriate state public service commission or other similar authority in the state in which the sale or delivery of power is made.
Anyone may submit comments, a protest, or a motion to intervene in accordance with the requirements of Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR 385.210, .211, .214, respectively. In determining the appropriate action to take, the Commission will consider all protests or other comments filed, but only those who file a motion to intervene in accordance with the Commission's Rules may become a party to the proceeding. Any comments, protests, or motions to intervene must be received on or before the specified comment date for the particular application.
The Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure require all intervenors filing documents with the Commission to serve a copy of that document on each person on the official service list for the project. Further, if an intervenor files comments or documents with the Commission relating to the merits of an issue that may affect the responsibilities of a particular resource agency, they must also serve a copy of the document on that resource agency.
Any filing must (1) bear in all capital letters the title “COMMENTS”, “PROTEST”, or “MOTION TO INTERVENE” as applicable; (2) set forth in the heading the name of the applicant and the project number of the application to which the filing responds; and (3) otherwise comply with the requirements of 18 CFR 385.2001 through 385.2005. All comments, motions to intervene, or protests must set forth their evidentiary basis. Any filing made by an intervenor must be accompanied by proof of service on all persons listed in the service list prepared by the Commission in this proceeding, in accordance with 18 CFR 385.2010.
                    The applications may be viewed on the Commission's website at 
                    http://www.ferc.gov/docs-filing/elibrary.asp
                     using the “eLibrary Search Form” link. Enter the docket number (P-943-152, P-943-153, and/or P-943-154) in the docket number field to access the document. For assistance, contact FERC Online Support at 
                    FERCOnlineSupport@ferc.gov
                     or toll-free at 1-866-208-3676, or for TTY, (202) 502-8659.
                
All comments must be filed by November 30, 2026, 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time.
                    The Commission strongly encourages electronic filing. Please file motions to intervene and protests using the Commission's eFiling system at 
                    https://ferconline.ferc.gov/FERCOnline.aspx.
                     Commenters can submit brief comments up to 10,000 characters, without prior registration, using the eComment system at 
                    https://ferconline.ferc.gov/QuickComment.aspx.
                     For assistance, please contact FERC Online Support at 
                    FERCOnlineSupport@ferc.gov,
                     (866) 208-3676 (toll free), or (202) 502-8659 (TTY). In lieu of electronic filing, please send a paper copy via U.S. Postal Service to: Debbie Anne A. Reese, Secretary, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, 888 First Street NE, Room 1A, Washington, DC 20426. Submissions sent via any other carrier must be addressed to: Debbie Anne A. Reese, Secretary, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, 12225 Wilkins Avenue, Rockville, Maryland 20852. The first page of any filing should include docket number P-943-152, P-943-153, and/or P-943-154.
                
                    For public inquiries and assistance with making filings such as interventions, comments, or requests for rehearing, contact the Office of Public Participation at (202) 502-6595 or 
                    OPP@ferc.gov.
                    For further information, contact Chris Chaney at (202) 502-6778 or 
                    christopher.chaney@ferc.gov.
(Authority: 18 CFR 2.1)
                    Dated: October 29, 2026.
Carlos D. Clay,
Deputy Secretary.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Information Collection Request Title:
Faculty Loan Repayment Program OMB No. 0906-0082—Revision.
Abstract:
HRSA administers the Faculty Loan Repayment Program (FLRP). FLRP provides health professionals from disadvantaged backgrounds, defined as a geographic and/or economic vulnerability, the opportunity to enter into a contract with HHS to receive repayment of qualifying educational loans in exchange for a minimum of 2 years of service as a full-time or part-time faculty member at an eligible health professions school. The applicant completes and submits an electronic application that identifies for the Secretary of HHS that the applicant comes from an economically or geographically vulnerable background, has a contract with an eligible health professions school to serve as a full-time or part-time faculty member for a minimum of 2 years, and has qualifying outstanding educational loans. In addition, for each undergraduate and/or graduate loan for which repayment is sought, the applicant is required to submit loan documentation verifying the establishment of the educational loan(s) and lender account statements, promissory notes including the original date, and current balance of the outstanding educational loan(s).
This revised ICR contains two new forms. The first is the Employer's Agreement to Loan Repayment Match/Request for a Waiver of the Loan Repayment Match form, which is needed to ensure applicant eligibility and school compliance with the statute. The second is the Semi-annual In-Service Verification form, which is sent to current participants and the institution twice each year to confirm their employment status. The addition of these forms and an increased number of respondents/applicants to the FLRP will increase the estimated burden hours.
This proposed ICR also contains updated terminology with respect to Disadvantaged Background and accompanying definitions by updating the following:
Changing form title to “Certification Regarding Vulnerable Background,”
Replacing “disadvantaged” with “vulnerable” throughout the form, and
Replacing “environmentally disadvantaged” with “geographically vulnerable.”
These changes are needed to align the form with the Administration's priority of reinforcing programs that direct resources to areas of greatest need to improve health outcomes. The FLRP statute defines eligible individuals as coming from “disadvantaged backgrounds” (42 U.S.C. 293b(a)) but does not define the term. HRSA's use of “vulnerable background” operationalizes the statutory term by identifying individuals whose geographic or economic circumstances inhibited their ability to obtain the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to enroll in and graduate from an eligible health professions school. This approach remains consistent with the statute's intent while incorporating more current terminology. These updates were made throughout the form to improve consistency and help ensure that applicants and reviewers understand the criteria using current terminology.
FLRP will define “vulnerable background” as “coming from a geographically vulnerable background or an economically vulnerable background that has inhibited the individual from obtaining the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to enroll in and graduate from an eligible health professions school.”
Examples of indicators that an individual comes from a geographically vulnerable background include, but are not limited to:
( printed page 69262)
Individuals who graduated from a high school with low average SAT/ACT scores or below-average state test results.
Individuals from a school district where 50 percent or less of graduates go to college.
Individuals raised in households where language barriers affected education access.
Individuals from a high school where at least 30 percent of enrolled students are eligible for free or reduced-price lunch.
Individuals who are the first generation in their family to attend college.
An individual from an economically vulnerable background is defined as someone who:
Comes from a low-income family. Low-income family is defined as a family that has an annual income below the 200 percent of the Department's poverty guidelines;
Is eligible for a Pell Grant; and/or
Comes from a family that receives public assistance (e.g.,
Temporary Assistance to Needy Families, Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, Medicaid, public housing).
The Secretary of HHS defines a `low-income family' for programs included in Titles III, VII, and VIII of the Public Health Service Act as having an annual income that does not exceed 200 percent of the Department's poverty guidelines, which are based on the U.S. Census Bureau's low-income threshold. This threshold is simplified to facilitate the determination of financial eligibility for some federal programs and further adjusted by the Secretary of HHS based on the Consumer Price Index. Family is defined a group of two or more individuals related by birth, marriage, or adoption who live together, or an individual who is not living with any relatives.

AGENCY:

ACTION:
Notice.
SUMMARY:
This notice announces that information submitted to EPA's Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics (OPPT) pursuant to the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA), including information that may be claimed as Confidential Business Information (CBI) by the submitter, will be transferred to or accessed by Avanti Corporation, in accordance with the CBI regulations. Avanti Corporation has
( printed page 69255)
been awarded a contract to perform work in connection with TSCA and access to this information will enable Avanti Corporation to fulfill the obligations of the contract.

For technical information contact:
Ira Lyons, New Chemicals Division (7405M), Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics, Environmental Protection Agency, 1200 Pennsylvania Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20460-0001; telephone number: (202) 566-1481; email address:
lyons.ira@epa.gov.
For general information:
The TSCA Assistance Information Service Hotline, Goodwill Vision Enterprises, 422 South Clinton Ave., Rochester, NY 14620; telephone number: (800) 471-7127 or (202) 554-1404; email address
: TSCA-Hotline@epa.gov.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. General Information
A. Does this action apply to me?
This action is directed to the public in general. This action may, however, be of interest to all who manufacture, process, or distribute industrial chemicals. Since other entities may also be interested, the Agency has not attempted to describe all the specific entities that may be affected by this action.
B. How can I get copies of this document and other related information?
EPA has established a docket for this action under
Docket ID no. EPA-HQ-OPPT-2003-0004. Publicly available docket materials are available electronically through
http://www.regulations.gov.
Additional instructions on commenting on and visiting the docket, along with more information about dockets generally, are available at
https://www.epa.gov/dockets.
II. What action is the agency taking?
Under Administrative and Technical Support for the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) New Chemical Program (NCP) solicitation number 47QRAA20D002D, task order number 68HERW27F0013, Avanti Corporation will perform technical and administrative tasks to support activities for the TSCA New Chemicals Program, including and not limited to: Tracking regulatory decisions, coordinating communications, preparing correspondences, drafting TSCA Section 5(e) and 5(f) Orders, sanitizing documents containing TSCA CBI, preparing information to be uploaded into ChemView, performing analyses, and other related tasks to support the program. In accordance with the requirements of 40 CFR 2.306(f), EPA has determined that the disclosure of CBI submitted to EPA under all sections of TSCA is necessary for Avanti Corporation to satisfactorily carry out the work required by the contract. Accordingly, Avanti Corporation personnel will be given access to information, including information submitted to EPA under all sections of TSCA, some of which may be claimed or determined to be CBI.
EPA is issuing this notice to inform all submitters that EPA will provide Avanti Corporation access to these CBI materials on a need-to-know basis only. All access to TSCA CBI under this contract takes place in accordance with EPA's
TSCA CBI Protection Manual.
Access to TSCA data, including CBI, will continue until October 31, 2029. If the contract is extended, this access will also continue for the duration of the extended contract without further notice. In accordance with the requirements of 40 CFR 2.306(f), the contract prohibits disclosure of information to a third party without prior written approval from the Agency.
Avanti Corporation personnel will sign nondisclosure agreements and will be briefed on appropriate security procedures before they are permitted access to TSCA CBI. Records of information provided to Avanti Corporation will be maintained by EPA project officers for this contract. All information supplied to Avanti Corporation by EPA for use in connection with this contract will be returned to EPA when Avanti Corporation has completed its work.

AGENCY:
Food and Nutrition Administration, U.S. Department of Agriculture.
                    ACTION:
Notice of approval to implement Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program demonstration project.
                    SUMMARY:
                        On September 15, 2026, the Food and Nutrition Administration (FNA) posted 
                        Federal Register
                         Number 2026-18880, which invited public comment on the State of Virginia's Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) demonstration project authorized under section 17(b) of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008. The comment period closed October 15, 2026. FNA has considered all comments received and is announcing its decision to proceed with approval of Virginia's request to implement its SNAP demonstration project.
                    
                    DATES:
The project is effective November 1, 2026.
            
                SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
                    Section 17(b) of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, 7 U.S.C. 2026(b), authorizes FNA to approve demonstration projects to test changes to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) that may increase programmatic efficiency and improve the delivery of SNAP benefits to raise levels of nutrition among eligible households. This demonstration project is implemented by the State, and FNA will carefully review the results of the project based on the State's evaluation data. All relevant documents, including the State's demonstration project request(s) and FNA approval(s), can be found in the supporting document section. Additionally, to support implementation and ensure transparency, FNA created a central web page on May 21, 2025, to post State agencies' project requests and approvals and provide exact implementation timelines. That web page is accessible at the following address: 
                    https://www.fna.usda.gov/snap/waivers/foodrestriction.
Discussion of Demonstration Project
State of Virginia Demonstration Project Request
                    The State of Virginia requested to conduct a demonstration project to amend the SNAP definition of food for purchase to exclude “sweetened beverages.” The State formally requested to conduct this project on November 4, 2025. On February 3, 2026, the State requested to modify the initial project request to amend the implementation date to October 1, 2026. Subsequently, in consultation with FNA, the State revised its planned implementation date to November 1, 2026. The State's project request and the subsequent modification request can be found in the supporting document section and on the FNA website at the following address: 
                    https://www.fna.usda.gov/snap/waivers/foodrestriction/virginia.
USDA Approval of Initial Demonstration Project Request
                    FNA approved the State's initial demonstration project request on December 10, 2025. The approval can be found in the supporting document section and at the following address: 
                    https://www.fna.usda.gov/snap/waivers/foodrestriction/virginia.
Discussion of Public Comments
FNA received 30 comments on Virginia's demonstration project request. Most commenters opposed the project, citing concerns about potential health and nutrition impacts, limits on participant choice, added burden on SNAP households, retailer and consumer confusion, and the project's evaluation measures. Supporters stated that the project advances SNAP's nutrition objectives, could improve public health outcomes, and would promote responsible use of taxpayer-funded benefits.
FNA carefully considered all comments and determined that none of the comments received were significant. FNA has decided to allow Virginia's revised project request to proceed without modification, effective November 1, 2026. SNAP's statutory purpose is to improve nutrition among low-income households, and FNA believes the project is consistent with that purpose and represents an appropriate policy intervention to address diet-related disease and obesity. FNA has supported the State in its efforts to prepare retailers and provide notice to SNAP households. FNA also notes that SNAP benefits are supplemental and do not restrict participants from purchasing excluded items with non-SNAP funds. FNA has determined that approval is authorized under section 17(b) of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 and that Virginia is prepared to implement the project successfully.
                    Shiela Corley,
Acting Administrator, Food and Nutrition Administration, USDA.

Notice is hereby given that the U.S. International Trade Commission has received a complaint entitled

October 29, 2026.
On October 16, 2026, Texas Stock Exchange LLC (“TXSE” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”), pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),[1]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder (“Rule 19b-4”),[2]
a proposed rule change to amend TXSE Rule 17.111(d) to modify the generic listing standards for Commodity-Based Trust Shares. The proposed rule change is described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons and is approving the proposed rule change (the “Proposal”), on an accelerated basis.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange filed a proposal to amend TXSE Rule 17.111(d), which governs the listing and trading of Commodity-Based Trust Shares. The Exchange proposes to adopt generic listing standards that would permit the Exchange to list and trade Commodity-Based Trust Shares pursuant to Rule 19b-4(e) under the Act without submitting a separate proposed rule change under Section 19(b) of the Act for each product. The proposed rule change would, among other things: (1) establish eligibility criteria for commodities, commodity-based assets, and securities held by a Trust; (2) permit up to 15% of the net asset value of the Trust's holdings to consist of certain digital commodities and securities that do not otherwise satisfy the applicable eligibility criteria; (3) permit actively managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares; and (4) establish related disclosure, liquidity, trading halt, firewall, surveillance, and other investor protection requirements. The text of the proposed rule change is provided in Exhibit 5.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in Sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
TXSE Rule 17.111(d) currently governs the listing and trading of Commodity-Based Trust Shares on the Exchange. Under the existing rule, the Exchange is required to submit a separate proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Act before listing Commodity-Based Trust Shares.[3]
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 17.111(d) to establish generic listing standards that would permit the Exchange to list and trade Commodity-Based Trust Shares that satisfy the requirements of Rule 17.111(d) pursuant to Rule 19b-4(e) under the Act. Commodity-Based Trust Shares that do not satisfy the applicable generic listing standards could continue to be listed
( printed page 69288)
pursuant to a separate proposed rule change under Section 19(b) of the Act.
Background
The proposed standards are substantially similar to generic listing standards previously approved by the Commission for Nasdaq, Cboe BZX, and NYSE Arca.[4]
In July 2026, the Commission approved amendments to Nasdaq's generic listing standards that, among other things, permit up to 15% of the net asset value (“NAV”) of a Trust's holdings to consist of certain digital commodities and securities that do not otherwise satisfy the applicable generic eligibility criteria, add a definition of “digital commodity,” and permit actively managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares, subject to additional safeguards. The Commission subsequently approved substantially similar amendments for NYSE Arca and Cboe BZX and materially identical amendments for Nasdaq Texas.[5]
The Exchange's proposal incorporates both the original generic listing standards and the subsequent amendments into Rule 17.111(d), with changes necessary to conform the Exchange's existing rule structure, definitions, and cross-references.
Proposal
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 17.111(d) to permit the Exchange to list and trade Commodity-Based Trust Shares that satisfy the requirements of Rule 17.111(d) pursuant to Rule 19b-4(e) under the Act. Rule 19b-4(e) provides that the listing and trading of a new derivative securities product by a self-regulatory organization is not deemed a proposed rule change pursuant to Rule 19b-4(c)(1) if the Commission has approved, pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Act, the self-regulatory organization's trading rules, procedures, and listing standards for the product class that would include the new derivative securities product and the self-regulatory organization has a surveillance program for the product class.[6]
Consistent with the Commission-approved generic listing standards, the Exchange would retain the ability to submit a proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Act to list and trade Commodity-Based Trust Shares that do not satisfy one or more of the applicable generic listing standards. The proposed rule would also provide that statements or representations contained in any such proposed rule change concerning (1) the description of the index, Trust holdings, or reference assets; (2) limitations on the index, Trust holdings, or reference assets; (3) the dissemination and availability of the index, Trust holdings, reference assets, or Intraday Indicative Values; or (4) the applicability of Exchange listing rules would constitute continued listing requirements. An issuer would be required to notify the Exchange of any failure to comply with such continued listing requirements. If the Commodity-Based Trust Shares do not satisfy those requirements, the Exchange may suspend trading and will initiate delisting proceedings under the TXSE Rule Series 16.500.
Definitions
The Exchange also proposes to modernize the definition of Commodity-Based Trust Shares in renumbered Rule 17.111(d)(3). October 29, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”) [1]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,[2]
notice is hereby given that on October 19, 2026, New York Stock Exchange LLC (“NYSE” or the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Exchange filed the proposal as a “non-controversial” proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act [3]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.[4]
The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 2(c) to restore language inadvertently omitted from the recently adopted definition of “associated person.” The proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
www.nyse.com
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 2 (“Member,” “Membership,” “Member Firm,” etc.) to restore language inadvertently omitted from the proposed definition of “associated person” in a recent rule filing.[5]
More specifically, the proposed change is a technical amendment that would ensure that the persons encompassed by the “approved person” category that the Exchange recently filed to delete are captured by the definition of “associated person” in Rule 2(c) for jurisdictional and all other applicable Exchange rules. The proposed rule change is not intended to effect any substantive change to the scope of the Exchange's jurisdiction.
Background and Proposed Rule Change
On September 18, 2026, the Exchange filed an immediately effective rule change to (1) eliminate the “approved person” registration category as no longer necessary, (2) adopt a new definition of “associated person” in Rule 2(c) based on the definition of associated person in Rule 1011(b) of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc. (“FINRA”) and elements of the current definition of approved person, and (3) make related technical and conforming changes.[6]
The Approved Person Filing is scheduled to become operative on October 18, 2026.[7]
As described in the Approved Person Filing, the Exchange did not intend to expand or narrow the scope of its jurisdiction. Rather, the proposal was designed to ensure that all persons currently encompassed by the approved person category would continue to be covered under the proposed definition of “associated person.” Specifically, the filing stated that proposed Rule 2(c)(3) would include the existing categories of approved persons: (i) persons that control a member organization; (ii) persons engaged in a securities or kindred business that is controlled by a member or member organization; and
( printed page 69286)
(iii) U.S. registered broker-dealers under common control with a member organization. The filing further explained that the proposed definition of “Control Person” was intended to encompass those same categories.[8]
The Exchange has since determined that the text of proposed Rule 2(c)(3), as filed, inadvertently omitted the clause covering persons engaged in a securities or kindred business that is controlled by a member or member organization. That clause appears in the Exchange's current approved person definition and was intended to be carried forward without substantive change. Consequently, the text of proposed Rule 2(c)(3) is inconsistent with both the description of the proposal and the Exchange's stated intent in the Approved Person Filing, which was to preserve, rather than modify, the existing scope of Exchange jurisdiction. AGENCY:
Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
ACTION:
Final rule.
SUMMARY:
The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC, agency, or Commission) is revising the agency's rules of practice and procedure to streamline contested adjudications in NRC licensing proceedings in response to the Accelerating Deployment of Versatile, Advanced Nuclear for Clean Energy Act of 2024 (ADVANCE Act) and Executive Order 14300, Ordering the Reform of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
DATES:
This final rule is effective on December 3, 2026, and applies to contested adjudicatory proceedings noticed on or after the effective date.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Executive Summary
A. Need for the Regulatory Action
The Accelerating Deployment of Versatile, Advanced Nuclear for Clean Energy Act of 2024 (ADVANCE Act) was signed into law in July of 2024. The ADVANCE Act establishes requirements to enhance the NRC's timeliness and efficiency, including a broad requirement for efficiency through an updated Mission Statement.[1]
As directly relevant to the hearing process, ADVANCE Act § 505(b) requires the NRC to provide “efficient and timely . . . proceedings” for a broad category of licensing actions, and ADVANCE Act § 207(c) requires the NRC (for certain reactor combined license applications) to, among other things, complete “any necessary public licensing hearings and related processes” not later than two years after docketing the application, to the maximum extent practicable.
Subsequently, the President directed a series of reforms to improve the agency's efficiency and effectiveness in the May 23, 2025, Executive Order (E.O.) 14300, “Ordering the Reform of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission” (90 FR 22587, May 29, 2025). As relevant to this final rule, section 5(j) of E.O. 14300 directs the NRC to streamline its public hearing process. Relatedly, E.O. 14300 section 5(a) directs the NRC to establish fixed deadlines for its evaluation and approval of specified licensing actions and requests, section 5(d) directs the NRC to establish an expedited approval pathway for reactor designs tested and demonstrated by the Department of Defense (also referred to as the Department of War (DOW)) [2]
or the Department of Energy (DOE), and section 5(e) directs the NRC to “[e]stablish a process for high-volume licensing of microreactors and modular reactors[.]”
In response to Congressional and Executive action, the NRC has developed this final rule focused on streamlining the agency's rules of practice and procedure. The changes to the contested hearing process will reduce burden, increase clarity, and promote efficiencies in line with deadlines established in accordance with the ADVANCE Act and E.O. 14300.
B. Major Provisions
Major provisions of this final rule include the following:
Revisions to the contested hearing process that will enable the NRC to generally complete adjudications within 11 to 13.5 months or faster for expedited proceedings.
A requirement for evidentiary hearings to begin as soon as practicable upon admission of contentions.
Strict deadlines for the completion of hearings.
Tailored hearing schedules that correspond to the staff's review schedule to the maximum extent practicable, considering the complexity of the application.
A reduction in discovery burden on all parties to focus on information of highest value and reflect the greater availability of information due to technological developments.
Revisions to accelerate Commission review of appeals.
Elimination, refinement, or addition of provisions that will accommodate the schedule directives of the ADVANCE Act andE.O. 14300.
C. Costs and Benefits
This final rule is considered to be a deregulatory action and will reduce burden for both the government and hearing participants by streamlining contested hearing proceedings. Over the five-year analysis period (2026-2030), the revisions to the contested hearing procedures are projected to yield savings for the public, the industry, and government. The combined net savings would generate cumulative undiscounted savings of $67.4 million. Using 2025 as the base year, the net present value (NPV) of these net savings is $61.7 million, discounted at 3 percent, or $55.2 million, discounted at 7 percent. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
                    This is a summary of the document of the Media Bureau's Order, in MB Docket No. 98-204, GN Docket No. 25-133, DA 26-1058, adopted and released on October 1, 2026. The full text of this document is available for public inspection online at 
                    https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DA-26-1058A1.pdf

                     Alternative formats are available for people with disabilities (Braille, large print, electronic files, audio format, etc.) and reasonable accommodations (accessible format documents, sign language interpreters, CART, etc.) may be requested by sending an email to 
                    fcc504@fcc.gov
                     or call the Consumer & Governmental Affairs Bureau at 202-418-0530 (voice), (202) 418-0432.
                
Synopsis
                    The Order of the Media Bureau of the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) conforms parts 73 and 74 of the Commission's rules to the decision of the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals (Fifth Circuit) in 
                    National Religious Broadcasters
                     v. 
                    FCC,
                     138 F.4th 282 (5th Cir. 2025), nullifying § 73.3612. In the 
                    Delete, Delete, Delete
                     proceeding, the Commission stated the goal of reviewing its rules “to identify and eliminate those that are unnecessary in light of current circumstances.” 
                    Delete, Delete, Delete,
                     GN Docket No. 25-133, Public Notice, 40 FCC Rcd 1601, 1601 (OMR 2025). Consistent with that goal, the Media Bureau finds § 73.3612 of the Commission's rules “no longer ha[s] any operative effect,” and therefore should not remain in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR).
                
                    Section 73.3612 of the Commission's rules, requiring broadcasters to annually submit information regarding their employees' race, ethnicity, and gender within specified job categories, was originally adopted in 1969 and has been suspended since 2001. In 2024, the Commission reinstated § 73.3612. 
                    Review of the Commission's Broadcast & Cable Equal Employment Opportunity Rules & Policies,
                     MB Docket No. 98-204, Fourth Report and Order and Order on Reconsideration, 39 FCC Rcd 1791, 1798-00, paras. 14-16 (2024). Parties appealed to the Fifth Circuit, challenging the reporting obligation, while § 73.3612 remained deferred. The Fifth Circuit subsequently found the “[t]he FCC lacks statutory authority to require broadcasters to submit employment data under Form 395-B,” 
                    National Religious Broadcasters,
                     138 F.4th at 296, and, as a result of the court vacating the Commission's 2024 order, the text of § 73.3612 that currently appears in the CFR, and references to § 73.3612 in the CFR, have no legal effect and are obsolete. Accordingly, the Media Bureau of the Commission deletes § 73.3612 and references to § 73.3612 from parts 73 and 74 of the Commission's rules, finding that doing so has no effect on the scope and nature of the currently enforceable Commission requirements and effectuates the Fifth Circuit's holding in 
                    National Religious Broadcasters.
                    Pursuant to the good cause exception under 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B), because we are simply conforming the text of the Commission's rules in the CFR to reflect the court's decision in 
                    National Religious Broadcasters,
                     and we are not taking any independent action or exercising any discretion, we find that notice and the opportunity for public comment are unnecessary for this action. For the same reason, pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 553(d), this action will be effective immediately upon publication in the 
                    Federal Register
                    .
                
                    The changes to parts 73 and 74 of the Commission's rules to conform to the Fifth Circuit decision in 
                    National Religious Broadcasters
                     are reflected in Appendix A.
                
                    Accordingly, 
                    it is ordered
                     that parts 73 and 74 of the Commission's rules, Title 47, are amended as set forth in Appendix A, effective upon publication in the 
                    Federal Register
                    .
                
This action is taken pursuant to the authority contained in sections 4(i), 4(j), and 155(c) of the Communications Act of 1934, as amended, 47 U.S.C. 154(i), 154(j), 155(c), and sections 0.61 and 0.283(e) of the Commission's rules, 47 CFR 0.61, 0.283(e).
The Bureau has determined, and the Administrator of the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs, Office of Management and Budget, concurs that this rule is non-major under the Congressional Review Act, 5 U.S.C. 804(2). The Commission will send a copy of this Order to Congress and the Government Accountability Office pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 801(a)(1)(A).
                    Federal Communications Commission
Thomas Horan,
Chief of Staff, Media Bureau.

(b) No application for renewal of license of any broadcast station will be considered unless there is on file with the FCC the information currently required by §§ 73.3613 through 73.3615, inclusive, for the particular class of station.

                Alphabetical Index [Amended]

                        Federal Register
                         on July 16, 2024. Following publication of this final rule, the EPA discovered an inadvertent error in the regulatory text and is correcting the error in this action.
                    
                    DATES:
The final rule is effective on November 3, 2026.
                    ADDRESSES:
                        The EPA has established a docket for this rulemaking under Docket ID No. EPA-HQ-OAR-2026-0725. All documents in the docket are listed on the
